purpose: The only place with the order of work steps: if (facts) then (stage, role, rule, gate, tool, ask). Facts and grammar: core/flow.schema.json

steps.why: Map from what you are about to do to the rule document that applies.
Set task_size, task_type, touches and unclear_requirements before choosing a path.
An unknown that changes the result is asked once, in one form with a recommended default, not guessed.
Big, architectural or unclear work gets a SPEC.md before any plan.
Agent configuration changes only after a backup and the owner's explicit yes.
Plan once with the high tier: impact note, ownership boundaries, acceptance checks.
Research the unknowns and check the owner's answers against the plan before implementation starts.
Search and fact gathering go to the cheap tier, never the router session.
Tests, reviews, search and mechanical edits go to the Codex subcontractor; code and maths stay with Claude.
Writing or changing code follows the code standard: contracts, reading order, comments, quality, domain rules.
Implementation from a complete brief goes to the standard tier in its own context.
The diff is scored by paths and size, never by a model's opinion; the level sets the verification depth.
A deterministic gate decides, not the author's confidence.
STANDARD and FULL risk add the full project quality gate.
Two failed attempts on a tier: stop, attach the evidence, move up one tier.
Two failed attempts on a tier: stop, attach the evidence, move up one tier.
The top tier needs an explained owner yes; after two failures on the high tier the owner decides.
Cheap deterministic checkers run before the commit and catch defects first.
FULL risk needs an independent reviewer on diff and spec, in a separate context.
Business changes touching auth, secrets, payments or external input get the security review.
Commit own paths only, with the project's finalizer when it has one.
After the commit: score HEAD (report-only), then log the outcome once so routing can learn.
